card.title: 1st AIRBORNE

card.flavorText: The 1st Parachute Brigade was part of the 1st Airborne Division of the British Army during WWII and participated in numerous operations and battles during the war. The first missions was in 1942, a parachute drop in France during Operation Biting, followed by a successful glider mission into Norway where they sabotaged Germany’s Heavy Water production. That same year the brigade was sent to North Africa where they fought as an independent unit, both as paratroopers and as normal infantry on the front line. This is where they earned their nickname the Red Devils. In 1943 the brigade participated in the Allied invasion of Sicily where they sustained heavy casualties in combat and were therefore held in reserves for the next couple of operations in Italy. In 1944 the brigade participated in the Battle of Arnhem as part of Operation Market Garden, and after heavy fighting and casualties the remaining members of the brigade were forced to surrender to the Axis forces. When the war ended they joined the 6th Airborne Division for security duties in Palestine.
